rationale.conceptual: The FLAPW method with spin-orbit coupling is a well-documented but non-trivial electronic-structure technique; successful reproduction requires understanding how to set up slab models, choose computational parameters, and interpret the total-energy difference for anisotropy. It is not a trivial cookie-cutter task but also not a brand-new algorithm.
rationale.execution: The workflow involves (i) generating five different slab structures with appropriate input files for FLAPW, (ii) performing semirelativistic self-consistent calculations and ensuring converged charge densities, (iii) running two separate relativistic diagonalizations per system, and (iv) extracting energies and computing MAE. This is a multi-stage scientific pipeline with dependencies, fragile tooling (FLEUR or similar FLAPW code), and requires handling convergence issues and parsing output files.

difficulty.reasoning: Reproducing magnetic anisotropy energies using FLAPW+SOC requires understanding the second-variation method, setting up slab geometries, and correctly running SCF and SOC calculations. This is a non-trivial but established method; the pipeline involves multi-step orchestration of an external scientific code with careful convergence and output parsing. The computational resources are moderate CPU-only work with small cells and no external data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: FLAPW calculations for small slab cells are CPU-only; peak memory is driven by wave-function storage in a typical plane-wave basis (16 GB is a safe upper bound). No external datasets are needed, only lattice parameters and structure coordinates.
